$comment: Wavee base culture — every user-facing UI string. Other cultures override per-key and fall back here. Keys flatten to a `Wavee.Strings` class via FluentGpu.SourceGen (Strings.Detail.Play == "detail.play"); parameterized keys expose a typed format method. `$unusedAllow` is analyzer-only (FLLOC005 keepers).

drag.$comment: Drag & drop CAPTIONS: what a drop will do (Add to X, Move into X) and, for a refusal, why it will not. A refusing drop target is TRANSPARENT to the engine (discovery walks past it), so the refusal ones are the only thing that tells the user why a drag was turned away — the drag chip shows them beside its not-allowed glyph.
drag.stillSyncing: Still syncing — try again in a moment
drag.$comment3: SIDEBAR ORGANISATION. The insertion line answers "where" for an ordinary before/after, so only the two slots it cannot express carry a sentence: an OUTDENT (the line jumps to a shallower depth) and the end of the whole tree. The four refusals below replace silent `return false`s that used to live three layers down in RootlistOps, where a folder dropped into its own descendant showed "Move into B" and then simply did nothing.
drag.organizeHint: Drop between playlists or onto a folder
drag.cantMoveIntoItself: Can’t move a folder into itself
drag.$comment2: The RESTING verb: what the chip says while the drag is travelling and no target is under the pointer. Most of a gesture is spent in that state, and without it the chip named only the song — so the drag never stated what it was FOR. Superseded per-target by the captions above the moment something accepts, and by a refusal reason when something refuses.
drag.dragOntoPlaylist: Drag onto a playlist to add
drag.$comment4: MULTI-SELECT + CREATE-BY-DROP. A rootlist drag may carry a whole selection (WaveeResourceDragPayload.RootlistItems), so every sentence that can name a count does — a 5-item filing reported in the singular reads as a move that only took one of them.

trackFacts.$comment: The expanded track row's details strip. It states EVERY fact the track carries at EVERY list width, because the table's own lanes are a function of width and drop Plays / BPM · Key / Added by / Date added as the list narrows. Labels are nouns, not sentences: each one sits above its value in a compact tile. Only present facts render — the sole — dash is the enrichment-pending state for tempo/key (extension kind 222) and stream counts (kind 185).
trackFacts.title: Track details
trackFacts.$comment2: Camelot encodes mode in its own suffix — the B ring is major, the A ring minor — so these two words are the only key wording we can state honestly. They are lowercase because they follow a tonic: "8B · C major".

likedFacts.$comment: The Liked Songs rail facts. Every one of these is derived from when tracks were SAVED — there is no play-recency copy here, because the play log is a 200-entry ring and could not answer it truthfully.
likedFacts.weekTip: {start} – {end} · {count, plural, one {# song liked} other {# songs liked}}
likedFacts.$comment3: The blend bar's TAIL. The five named slices end in a disclosure button that opens the card in place: the tail is redrawn at full width with its own legend, so a descriptor worth 3% of the library is a real, clickable segment instead of six pixels. tailShareTip's share is of the TAIL (the bar it labels), every other share here is of the tagged likes.

likedFacts.underFloor: … and {count, plural, one {# descriptor} other {# descriptors}} under 1 %
likedFacts.lastYear: {count, plural, one {# song} other {# songs}} you liked this week last year
likedFacts.$comment2: The rail facts are LENSES over the track list: a bar, a face and a blend slice each filter the list to what they describe. weekRange is the single source of the week wording, shared by the bar tooltip and the list header so the two cannot name different weeks.
likedFacts.artistTip: {artist} · {count, plural, one {# liked song} other {# liked songs}}
likedFacts.weekTipAdded: {start} – {end} · {count, plural, one {# song added} other {# songs added}}
likedFacts.$comment4: Which facts EARN a card (LikedFactsRules.Shape): a distribution renders as the GRAPH card when it has a shape, as a one-line LABEL pill when one value dominates or the evidence is thin, and not at all when it cannot be answered honestly. Pills are lenses too — a pill names exactly the filter it applies. Tempo is Spotify's kind-222 BPM; half/double-time reporting (87 vs 174) is real, so a tempo pill names the BAND it filters and never says 'steady'.
likedFacts.pillTempoTip: median {median} bpm · {known} of {total} tracks have a tempo
likedFacts.pillYearsTip: {range} · {count, plural, one {# track} other {# tracks}} of {known} dated
likedFacts.$comment5: THE INSIGHTS SHEET. In the stacked (vertical) arm there is no rail, so the bento above is reached through a dismissable sheet laid over the list instead of falling to the bottom of the page. sheetTitle heads the panel; sheetOpen labels the toolbar toggle that opens it (and reads as the name of what is behind the button, not as a verb); sheetClose is its ×.

play.$comment2: The two halves of the player bar's behind-the-edge button, kept separate because they are two different jobs: goLive is the VERB (a caps word-mark that matches the LIVE chip beside it), behind is the COUNT, whose leading character is U+2212 MINUS SIGN — the typographic minus, not a hyphen — so it lines up with the digits either side of it. `time` arrives already formatted as m:ss / h:mm:ss.

modulePage.$comment: A page a playback module DESCRIBES and the app renders (Part 9). `title` is the destination's fallback label — used by the tab strip, the breadcrumb and a pinned row when the navigating surface carried no name of its own. `openOn` takes the module's display name ({name}), so the row reads 'Open on YouTube'. There is deliberately no `loading` and no `retry` here: the loading state is a shimmer DERIVED from the page itself and carries no copy at all, and the retry label is the app's one `common.retry` (ErrorState owns it) — a second spelling of either would be a dead key that drifts. `playing` is the WATCH layout's inert state capsule — it replaces the play capsule while this page's entity is the item in the bar, so it is a state badge and never a control.

tip.title: Pick your visualizer
tip.body: Nineteen styles, all tinted from the album art. Choose one on the right, or press [ and ] to step through them. Wavee hides the controls after three seconds; move the mouse to bring them back.

vizSub.tunnel: Frames fly past on the beat
vizSub.mosaic: Covers that flip on the beat

vizTip.verse: The song's own words, landing as they are sung, in the album's colours.
vizTip.bloom: The album art floats over soft clouds of its own colours that swell with the music.
vizTip.bars: Forty rounded bars, mirrored from the centre, with peaks that fall back slowly.
vizTip.ring: The spectrum circles the cover, and a ring ripples out on every beat.
vizTip.orbit: Three arcs sweep with the bass, the mids and the highs around the tempo.
vizTip.aurora: Three slow ribbons of light rise with the low, middle and high bands.
vizTip.timeline: The whole song's waveform with the beats ticking past the playhead.
vizTip.classic: A segmented spectrum of lit glass cells, after the Winamp classic.
vizTip.warp: A starfield that rushes forward when the bass hits.
vizTip.tunnel: Rounded frames fly toward you, a new one on every beat.
vizTip.ambience: Glowing orbs drift in orbit, each one swelling with its own band.
vizTip.kaleido: A six-fold kaleidoscope of light that turns with the mids.
vizTip.scope: The sound wave itself, drawn as a soft glowing line.
vizTip.drift: A ring of light that leaves fading trails as it spins and pulses.
vizTip.type: The artist, title and album as giant words drifting across the stage.
vizTip.mosaic: A wall of covers from your queue and recent plays that flip on the beat.
vizTip.spotlight: The artist's photos with slow pans that change every eight bars.
vizTip.magneto: Charged particles of light pushed and pulled by the music.
vizTip.flow: A wave of light bent into slow currents, after G-Force.

settings.title: Full screen

settings.sensitivitySub: How strongly the visualizers react to the music
settings.lyricsOverlaySub: Show the current line over the visualizer
settings.syncOffsetSub: Shift the visualizers earlier or later to match what you hear — Bluetooth headphones usually need a positive value
settings.calmSub: Calmer visualizers: smaller swings, a softer beat, no flashes
settings.momentsSub: Every eight bars, on the downbeat, the visualizer turns to the album art's next colour
